fatal_errors: The hypothesis predicts improved elevated-temperature tensile behavior after LAM, but the reported high-temperature tensile tests established temperature-dependent softening of the alloy rather than a LAM-versus-CM tensile-performance improvement.
It describes the starting alloy as single-phase even though the measured microstructure contained BCC A2, BCC B2, and Ti2Ni phases.
explanation: The intervention, machining parameters, baseline, softening mechanism, and principal discriminating measurements closely reconstruct the target. It correctly links localized heating near 800 °C to reduced cutting resistance, less work hardening, larger retained grain size, and improved surface condition. However, it conflates improved machinability with demonstrated improvement in elevated-temperature tensile properties; the latter was not established by a post-LAM versus post-CM comparison. It also overstates the material as single-phase, applies argon conditions too broadly when argon specifically concerned thermal-property measurements, omits the reported 930/980/800 °C optimum inconsistency, and provides no supporting evidence citations or quantitative prior results. The proposed controlled comparison is strongly falsifiable for machining outcomes, but its tensile component tests an extrapolation rather than a reported result.
